version.description: Which version of this format the file is written in.

presets.description: Your presets, by name. Each lists only what it changes from the defaults.

background.description: What's behind the text. A video: "pool" (built in) or a path to a video file. Or one of: "color", the theme's background color; "gradient" and "gel" (a slowly churning nebula), in the theme's colors unless [presets.<name>.gradient] or [presets.<name>.gel] say otherwise; "clear", "frosted glass" and "liquid glass", showing the desktop through the window.

font.description: The typeface: the name of an installed font ("Menlo", "JetBrains Mono", or a specific face such as "Menlo Bold"), "Monaspace Neon" (bundled), or a path to a font file. Characters the font lacks come from Monaspace Neon, then the system's fonts.

font_size.description: Text size, in points. View > Bigger and Smaller change it for one window, and Default Size returns to this. 6 to 72.

exposure.description: Brightness of the background video. 0 to 2.

hue_shift.description: Rotates the background video's colors, in degrees. 0 to 360.

crt.description: The CRT effect: scanlines, curvature and glow.

hdr_text.description: Draw text brighter than SDR white on HDR displays.

ligatures.description: Draw pairs like -> and != as single symbols.

typing_animation.description: Animate output as it is typed onto the screen.

theme.description: The color theme: text, the cursor, the selection, and the colors programs use. Any of its colors can be changed in [presets.<name>.colors].

foreground.description: Text color, as "#rrggbb". Empty uses the theme's.

background.description: The background color: what background = "color" fills the window with and the glass kinds are tinted by, what programs paint with, and what sink reports to programs that ask whether it's light or dark. A video shows through it. Empty uses the theme's.

cursor.description: Cursor color. Empty uses the theme's.

selection.description: Selection highlight, drawn translucently over what's behind it. Empty uses the theme's.

palette.description: The 16 colors programs choose from: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, then their bright versions. A shorter list replaces just the first colors; the rest stay the theme's.

colors.description: For background = "gradient": its colors, in order, evenly spaced. Empty runs from the theme's background toward its blue.

angle.description: Which way the gradient runs, in degrees: 0 is left to right, 90 top to bottom, 45 top-left to bottom-right. 0 to 360.

colors.description: For background = "gel": five colors from the darkest depths to the brightest wisps. Empty uses the theme's (sink's own theme gives the original purple).

speed.description: How fast the gel churns. 0 holds it still. 0 to 4.

tint.description: For the clear and glass backgrounds: how much of the theme's background color is laid over them, so text stays readable. 0 is none. 0 to 1.

include.description: Other files to read first, such as shared themes or settings for one machine. Each is a base: the next file, and finally this one, override what it sets. Paths are relative to the file naming them; Settings only ever changes this file.

preset.description: The preset in use: a built-in such as "pool", or the name of one of your [presets.<name>] tables.

scrollback_lines.description: Lines of output kept above the screen, per pane. 100 to 1000000.

integration.description: Load sink's shell integration into zsh and bash: prompt marks (OSC 133) and the working directory (OSC 7), which make Cmd+Up/Down prompt jumping and new tabs in the current directory work.

command.description: The program to run in new terminals: a path, or a name such as "fish" (found on PATH, in Homebrew's folders or in /etc/shells). Empty runs your login shell.

args.description: Arguments for it, after -l if login is on.

login.description: Start it as a login shell (-l), so it reads your login startup files. Turn off for a command that isn't a shell, such as tmux.

working_directory.description: Where new terminals start. Empty is your home folder. New tabs and splits still start where the shell beside them is, when it says.

env.description: Environment variables to set for it, as a table: [shell.env] then NAME = "value" lines.

keybindings.description: Keys and what they do. Move an action to a key, free a key with "none", or make a key send text. Keys are written "cmd+shift+d" or as menus show them, "⌘⇧D".

option_as_meta.description: Make Option act as Meta, sending ESC before the key (for emacs and readline shortcuts) instead of typing special characters. true for both Option keys, or "left" or "right" for just one.
